# Page 27^page=27
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 27 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Union Minister Manohar Lal Khattar Launches Operational Guidelines for Urban Challenge Fund In April 2026, Union Minister Manohar Lal Khattar, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), launched the Operational Guidelines for Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) along with the Credit Repayment Guarantee Sub-Scheme (CRGSS) in New Delhi, Delhi, to strengthen urban infrastructure financing and make cities investment-ready. • The UCF aims to transform cities into financially sustainable growth hubs aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 and broader urban transformation goals. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of Operational Guidelines for UCF along with CRGSS ✓ By Whom? Union Minister Manohar Lal Khattar, MoHUA ✓ Total Corpus: Rs 1 lakh crore (Central Assistance) ✓ Target Catalytic Investment: Rs 4 lakh crore. ✓ Funding pattern: CA limited to 25% of project cost; at least 50% from market-based sources ✓ Implementation period: FY26 to FY31 ✓ CRGSS allocation: Rs 5,000 crore (for smaller cities) ✓ Focus sectors: Redevelopment, urban mobility, water-sanitation, climate-resilient infrastructure. ✓ Other Initiatives: Digital Platform E-directory; MoUs & LoIs signed. About Urban Challenge Fund (UCF): Background: In February 2026, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved the UCF, a major initiative aimed at strengthening urban infrastructure financing. • It is a central government initiative designed to provide financial support and catalyze market- based investments for developing sustainable, resilient, and growth-oriented urban infrastructure in cities. Implementation: Implemented runs from Financial Year 2025–26(FY26) to FY31, extendable up to FY34. Finance: Total Central Assistance of Rs. 1 lakh crore is structured to catalyze nearly Rs. 4 lakh crore in total urban investments. Funding Pattern: The Central Government support will be limited to 25% of the project cost, while at least 50% of the funding will be raised through municipal bonds, bank loans, and Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs), ensuring financial discipline and promoting private sector participation. Allocation: Rs. 90,000 crore is allocated for project funding and Rs. 5,000 crore for capacity building and preparation. Focus: Key areas include redevelopment, urban mobility, non-motorised transport, water and sanitation, and climate-resilient infrastructure. About Credit Repayment Guarantee Sub-Scheme (CRGSS): Overview: CRGSS is a dedicated component of the UCF that supports smaller cities by providing credit guarantees to help them access and raise finance from market-based sources. Allocation: Rs.5,000 crore is earmarked under UCF for this sub- scheme. Benefits: The scheme strengthens creditworthiness, reduces lender risk, prioritizes Tier-II and Tier-III cities including hilly and North-Eastern Regions (NERs), and enhances financial inclusion while empowering ULBs to become investment-ready and support broader urban infrastructure development.

Exam Hint: ✓ What? Patent filings in India increased by 30.2% in FY26 ✓ Total Filings: 1,43,729 ✓ Announced by: Union Minister Piyush Goyal, MoC&I ✓ Global Rank: 6th (WIPO) ✓ Domestic Share: 69.4% (99,721 filings) ✓ Top States: TN, Karnataka, Maharashtra ✓ Top Sectors: Computers, Mechanical, Chemistry ✓ Law: Patents Act, 1970 About Patent Filings in India: Sector-wise Distribution: In FY26, the highest number of patent filings were recorded in computer-related fields, followed by mechanical engineering, chemistry, communication, and electronics sectors. Growth: This rise continues a steady upward trend since FY17, when filings stood at 45,444, indicating growing innovation and research activities. Global Ranking: India ranks 6th globally in patent filings as per the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO). • Among foreign applicants, the United States of America (USA) leads, followed by Japan, South Korea, and China. However, their combined share is less than one-third of total filings in India. Rise in Domestic Filings: Domestic patent filings increased to 99,721 in FY26 from 68,201 in FY25, raising their share to 69.4% from 61.8%. • Key contributors include states such as Tamil Nadu (TN), Karnataka, and Maharashtra, along with increasing participation from educational institutions, startups, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), and Research and Development (R&D) institutions. Decline in Patent Grants: Despite the surge in applications, patent grants declined by 36%, dropping to 21,439 in FY26 from 33,501 in FY25, reflecting stricter examination and quality control measures.

# Page 33^page=33
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 33 Daily Content PDF ✓ Abroad Office: Representative offices abroad requires RBI approval Key Highlights Applicable to: The directions are applicable across various categories of NBFCs, including deposit taking NBFCs, Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) and Investment and Credit Companies (NBFC-ICCs), NBFC-MFI (Microfinance Institutions), NBFC-IFC (Infrastructure Finance Companies) and etc Sections: Accordingly, in exercise of the powers conferred under Chapter IIIB of the RBI Act, 1934, and Section 30A of the National Housing Bank (NHB) Act, 1987, the RBI issues to every NBFC the Amendment Directions. Effective from: The amendment directions shall come into force with immediate effect. Application submission: Applications must be submitted through the PRAVAAH (Platform for Regulatory Application, Validation And AutHorisation) portal. Branch Expansion Conditions: The conditions for opening branches for Deposit taking – NBFCs are: • Up to Rs 50 Crores (Cr): Deposit-taking NBFCs with net owned funds (NOF) up to Rs 50 cr or with lower credit ratings are permitted to open branches only within the state of their registered office. • Above Rs 50 Cr: If its NOF is more than Rs 50 cr and its credit rating is AA or above, then it may open a branch or appoint agents anywhere in India. • Below AA: An NBFC with NOF greater than Rs 50 cr and credit rating below AA, shall be eligible to open branches only within the home state where its registered office is situated. Entity Specific Norms HFC: The directions also specify that HFCs must inform the NHB before opening branches in India, and are not permitted to open branches abroad. NBFC-ICCs: These NBFCs engaged in lending against gold collateral must obtain prior approval from the RBI for opening more than 1000 branches and are required to ensure adequate storage and security facilities for pledged gold. Operational Guidelines Expansion Approval: NBFCs must notify the RBI before expanding branches. • If no objection is raised within 30 days, they may proceed. Branch Closure: The guidelines also cover closure of branches, mandating that NBFCs provide at least 3 months’ public notice in newspapers and inform the RBI or NHB accordingly. Abroad offices: Additionally, opening representative offices abroad requires prior RBI approval and such offices are restricted to liaison and research activities without any fund outflows.
